mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES at t-0w reflects fewer commuting trips, which reduces incidental shopping before and after work. If that commuter loss persists, RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -25 and TRANSIT remains below -35 for most of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCER Y_PHARM after a prior dip would indicate more routine local errand activity, and those trips substitute for discretionary retail visits. That substitution should push RETAIL_REC downward within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2 after being below -5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days even after GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -2 from a prior week below -5.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weaken at the same time, the city loses both commuting flows and pass-through retail exposure. That joint contraction should produce lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks than over the previous four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remaining materially below their prior four-week average.

mechanism_narrative: If a mobility restriction regime is active, the large contemporaneous fall in TRANSIT will translate into fewer discretionary shopping trips and weaker retail visits with a short lag. Under that regime, RETAIL_REC should fall within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops more than 10 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stays above +10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move lower in the week after TRANSIT falls sharply while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility indicates better leisure-weather conditions and shifts trips toward outdoor destinations. That seasonal diversion should reduce retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken over 28 days even though PARKS remains higher than its prior month average.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL together with falling TRANSIT implies people are staying closer to home and making fewer discretionary outings. That home-centered pattern should lower retail mobility over a four-week horizon.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and TRANSIT stays depressed.

mechanism_narrative: The abrupt drop in WORKPLACES at t-0w marks a fresh shock, and retail footfall typically follows commuting activity with a one- to two-week lag. If the shock is real, RETAIL_REC should be lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after WORKPLACES posts a week-on-week drop larger than 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: If mobility restrictions ease, the combination of rising TRANSIT and WORKPLACES will restore mixed-purpose trips and shopping opportunities. Under that reopening regime, RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -35 and WORKPLACES rises above -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over 28 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES cross above their stated thresholds.
